copy.blurb: Australia enters this World Cup with momentum the market hasn't fully priced. The Socceroos are valued at just 27% to win, while the model — which leans on recent form and comparable strength — rates them at 36%. That 8.6-point gap is substantial enough to merit attention. Part of the disconnect lies in how the market has weighted tournament history; Australia has never won a knockout match at a World Cup, a shadow that still hangs over their odds despite significant recent shifts in setup. But the Guardian reported that Tony Popovic "has brought discipline and structure as the Socceroos target their first knockout win in a World Cup," and the team showed that structure in action just before selection — they "appear to have found something more important: confidence," according to the Guardian's report on their latest preparation. That form signal, fresh and concrete, is exactly what the model captures but the market seems to have discounted. Paraguay's Elo rating sits just 10 points below Australia's, making them genuine opponents; still, the 17-point swing in Australia's favour (from 27% market to 36% model) suggests the Socceroos are worth a closer look at the current price.
